questions.q: What distinguishes session security (this lesson) from everything covered in Chapters 1-3?
options: Chapters 1-3 cover what a logged-in user can see and do; session security is about whether the authenticated connection itself is secure
Session security is just another name for field-level security
Session security replaces the need for OWD and sharing rules
There is no meaningful difference
questions.explain: The lesson frames session security as a distinct, underlying layer — independent of what permissions a user holds once authenticated.

questions.q: What is the tradeoff with locking a session to its originating IP address?
options: There is no downside — it should always be enabled
It only works for guest users
It stops a stolen session token from being replayed elsewhere, but can break sessions for legitimately mobile users who switch networks
It disables MFA automatically
questions.explain: IP locking is a real defense against session hijacking, but the lesson is explicit about its cost: legitimate users switching networks mid-session can get disrupted.

questions.q: What does a High Assurance session requirement let an admin do?
options: Automatically log out all users after one hour
Grant View All to any user who completes MFA
Replace the need for a Session Timeout setting
Require a stronger authentication level for specific sensitive actions, even if the user's normal session only reached Standard assurance
questions.explain: High Assurance narrows which authentication strength is acceptable for specific sensitive actions, independent of the user's regular login session.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what is the status of MFA for direct UI logins in Salesforce?
options: It is an optional best practice admins can choose to enable
It has been required org-wide since 2022 — a platform baseline, not an optional setting
It only applies to guest users
It was deprecated in favor of IP locking
questions.explain: The lesson states MFA has been mandatory for direct UI logins since 2022, making it a baseline rather than a best-practice suggestion.

questions.q: What does the Health Check dashboard do?
options: It compares an org's actual security settings against Salesforce's recommended baseline, scores it, and allows fixing many findings in one click
It only checks field-level security settings
It automatically enforces MFA on all users
It is a manual, non-automated checklist with no scoring
questions.explain: Health Check provides an automated, scored comparison to Salesforce's baseline recommendations, with one-click remediation for many settings — described in the lesson as the automated cousin of a manual audit.
